title: Did Trump FIX Soybeans?? Record Demand Projected, China Is Buying

bullets: Dec corn -1 3/4 at 4.47; Jan beans +3 1/4 at 12.20; Dec SRW +1/4 at 6.06 3/4; Dec KC -1 1/4 at 6.44 3/4; Dec spring -1 at 6.24 3/4
Inspections wk to Oct 29: beans 90 mbu (-2.3% w/w, YTD +56% y/y); corn 35 mbu (+39% w/w, YTD -13%); wheat 3 mbu, record weekly low, -61% w/w, YTD -36%
Bean shipments to China 5.98 MMT MYTD (vs 0 last yr, 5.76 two yrs ago); ~8 MMT incl. this week
Bean export sales +80% y/y, shipments +56% vs USDA +11.8%; USDA likely too low; total bean demand at record even on USDA number
Flash sales: 68 mbu corn to Mexico (45 old crop / 23 new crop); 5 mbu beans to China
Corn export sales still -34% y/y; hosts think USDA corn export estimate likely too high
China soyoil stocks record ~1.5 MT (+4.3% y/y) as crush outpaces weak demand; soyoil exports ~3x y/y to ~800k t (9M)
Chinese trade negotiator met US ag delegation Monday; non-soy US ag purchases tracking 7-yr low (Reuters) vs ~$17B non-soy commitment claimed by White House (not in writing)
Mon: Jan beans -~18c to ~12.17, lowest settle since mid-Aug (crude drop, fund liquidation, strong yields); Dec corn +1c ~4.48; wheat slightly higher on Russia-Ukraine strikes
Funds est. sold ~15k beans net Monday, still ~176k long
Hosts read bean weakness as market pricing a bigger US crop; possible USDA yield hike next week
Corn: fresh overnight lows, funds likely still liquidating; farmer selling light and slowing on breaks
SRW: market ignoring Black Sea; no US demand pickup; ideas of big winter wheat acres (next report Jan 12)
Corn harvest 74% (prior 60, 5y 77, trade 73); beans 88% (prior 79, 5y 84, in line); winter wheat planted 83% (prior 76, 5y 84, trade 86)
Corn by state: IA 66 vs 79 avg (too wet); IL 86 vs 83; OH 53 vs 60; MN 82 vs 85; ND 76 ahead; SD 63 vs 75; NE 66 vs 75
Market focus shifting to Brazil
AgRural: Brazil beans 53% planted (prior 40, LY 47); 1st-crop corn 63% (prior 58, LY 59)
Last 7d drier than normal across most bean areas, helped wet south dry out; no delays
Euro 1-7d: Mato Grosso ~61% of normal rain, heavy again in Parana/south; 8-14d wetter north, drier south; no concern, price action confirms
Mon: live cattle slightly lower most months; feeders +$0.65 to +$1.43
S&P -10; Treasuries lower (yields up); Dec WTI recovering after Monday selloff
Election day; hosts see little direct market impact. No Fed/rates commentary beyond the Treasury move
